name: Pumpkin seed (Cucurbita pepo)
short: Pumpkin seed allergy is rare but often severe: anaphylaxis in 64% of 25 children (case series). Men: fewer adverse events than an alpha-blocker (prostate, 1 trial); seed oil like placebo (hair loss).
text: Pumpkin seed allergy is described as rare but potentially severe: in a case series of 25 children with IgE-mediated pumpkin seed allergy at one clinic, all had immediate reactions and 64% had anaphylaxis, most had other allergic conditions and many were also allergic to tree nuts or other seeds, and a literature search in the same report found 14 previously published cases, mostly adults, 57% with anaphylaxis; a separate case report describes anaphylaxis to pumpkin seed in an 8-year-old boy. These reports concern eating the seeds; the abstracts do not say whether seed extracts or oil carry the same allergy risk. In a meta-analysis of 8 randomized controlled trials of pumpkin seed in 2,170 men with benign prostatic hyperplasia, adverse events were fewer with pumpkin seed than with an alpha-blocker in one head-to-head trial, but the abstract does not report how adverse events compared with placebo, and the authors rated certainty low to very low. In a 24-week placebo-controlled trial of pumpkin seed oil in 76 men with hair loss, adverse effects did not differ between groups. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
